citeAs: Huang, Y., Bai, Y., Zhu, Z., Zhang, J., Zhang, J., Su, T., Liu, J., Lv, C., Zhang, Y., Lei, J., Fu, Y., Sun, M., & He, J. (2023). C-E VAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models. NeurIPS 2023 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks.
creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He (Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Tsinghua University; University of Edinburgh; The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)
description: C-E VAL is a comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite for foundation models consisting of 13,948 multiple-choice exam questions across 52 disciplines and four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional. It is designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities in a Chinese context, and includes a harder subset called C-E VAL HARD.
name: C-E VAL
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The questions underwent several rounds of human validation by the authors, and all LaTeX notations were checked to ensure they compiled without syntax errors.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Documents were parsed into a structured multiple-choice format automatically when possible and otherwise manually by the authors. For subjects with complex mathematical notation, the authors manually converted expressions into standard LaTeX. Questions were processed to include exactly four choices, and the data then underwent several rounds of human validation by the authors. For development examples, GPT-4 first generated step-by-step explanations for the ground-truth answer and the authors manually revised those explanations.
rai:dataBiases: The authors explicitly note that English benchmarks exhibit geographical biases toward the domestic knowledge of the regions that produce them, and C-E VAL is designed to evaluate knowledge relevant to Chinese users, such as Chinese culture, history, and laws. They also describe efforts to mitigate data contamination by collecting from mock exams or small-scale local exams rather than exact national exam questions widely available online.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed from real-world, challenging human exams in China. The primary source is mock exams freely available on the internet; some college-level questions are past exam questions from top universities publicly shared by students; and around 2,000 college questions come from mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam sourced from the Weipu website with authorization.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consisted primarily of exam questions in PDF or Microsoft Word documents and a minor fraction as web pages. Most samples were sourced from PDF or Microsoft Word documents on the internet rather than directly from plain text or structured questions.
rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that C-E VAL, along with English-language benchmarks, is far from perfect for LLM evaluation. It does not cover many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, and it does not assess aspects beyond accuracy including safety, bias, and robustness.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were manipulated post-collection to ensure exactly four choices: questions with fewer than four options were removed, and for questions with more than four options, incorrect choices were randomly dropped. The dataset was also split into development, validation, and test sets within each subject.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents were initially processed into text. Questions were parsed into a structured format automatically when possible and otherwise manually. Complex mathematical notation was manually converted into standard LaTeX. All questions were normalized to exactly four choices by eliminating questions with fewer than four options and randomly dropping incorrect choices for questions with more than four options. The data also underwent deduplication and cleaning, and the questions were randomly split within each subject into development, validation, and test sets, with validation and test created at a 1:9 ratio and five development exemplars per subject.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors anticipate that C-E VAL will foster the development and growth of foundation models for Chinese users by helping analyze model strengths and shortcomings in a Chinese context.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended to evaluate advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context, help developers understand model strengths and shortcomings from multiple dimensions, support answer-only and few-shot chain-of-thought evaluation, and serve as a suite of benchmarks whose subsets can be used to assess specific model abilities.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to automatically generate step-by-step explanations for the development split before human revision.
